## Scope and Interpretation

## 1.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.1] Section I of this practice direction contains general provisions about proceedings in the High Court under Parts 5 and 8 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 and Parts 4A and 5  of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (External Requests and Orders) Order 2005. ## 1.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] Section II contains provisions about applications to the High Court under Part 5 of the Act and Part 5 of the Order in Council for –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] (a) a recovery order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] (b) a property freezing order or (where applicable) a prohibition order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] (c) an interim receiving order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] (d) a management receiving order under section 245E of the Act or Article 150A of the Order in Council (as appropriate); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2] (e) the registration of external orders. ## 1.2A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2A] Section IIA contains provisions about applications to the High Court under Part 4A of the Order in Council for –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2A] (a) a prohibition order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.2A] (b) a management receiving order under Article 141I of the Order in Council. ## 1.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] Section III contains provisions about applications to the High Court for—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (a) an unexplained wealth order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (b) an interim freezing order (see paragraph 1.5(15));

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (c) a management receiving order in connection with an interim freezing order under section 362N of the Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (d) applications under Part 8 of the Act for any of the following types of order or warrant in connection with a civil recovery investigation, and applications to the High Court under Part 1 of the 2013 Order for any of the following types of order or warrant in connection with an external investigation—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (i) a production order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (ii) a search and seizure warrant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (iii) a disclosure order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (iv) a customer information order; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.3] (v) an account monitoring order. ## 1.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.4] Section IV of this practice direction contains further provisions about applications for each of the specific types of order and warrant listed in paragraph 1.3 above. ## 1.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] In this practice direction –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (1) ‘the Act’ means the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (2) ‘appropriate officer’ has the meaning set out in section 378 of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (3) ‘appropriate person’ has the meaning set out in section 352(5) or section 353(10) of the Act (as appropriate);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (4) for the purposes of section II ‘enforcement authority’ has the meaning set out in section 316 of the Act, and for the purposes of sections III and IV ‘enforcement authority’ has the meaning set out in section 362A(7) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (5) ‘the Order in Council’ means the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (External Requests and Orders) Order 2005;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (6) ‘the 2013 Order” means the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (External Investigations) Order 2013;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (7) ‘civil recovery proceedings’ means proceedings under Part 5 of the Act or Part 5 of the Order in Council (as appropriate);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (8) ‘’interim receiving order’ has the meaning set out in section 246 of the Act or Article 151 of the Order in Council (as appropriate);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (9) ‘management receiver’ means a receiver appointed by order of the court under any of the provisions listed in paragraph (4B);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (10) ‘management receiving order’ means an order to appoint a receiver:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (a)for the purposes of Section II, under section 245E of the Act or Article 150 of the Order in Council;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (b)for the purposes of Section IIA, under Article 141I of the Order in Council;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (c)for the purposes of Section III (where the order relates to an Interim Freezing Order), under section 362N of the Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (11) ‘management receiving order’ means an order to appoint a receiver under section 245E of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (12) ‘property freezing order’ has the meaning set out in section 245A of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (13) ‘prohibition order’ has the meaning set out in article 141D of the Order in Council;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (13A) ‘responsible officer’ has the meaning set out in section 362A(8) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (14) ‘unexplained wealth order’ has the meaning set out in section 362A(3) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (15) ‘interim freezing order’ has the meaning set out in section 362J(3) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (16) ‘the Regulations’ means the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (Legal Expenses in Civil Recovery Proceedings) Regulations 2005;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (17) ‘relevant authority’ has the meaning set out in section 357(7) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (18) ‘relevant Director’ has the meaning set out in section 352(5A) of the Act;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (19) ‘CPR’ means the Civil Procedure Rules 1998; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 1.5] (20) other expressions used have the same meaning as in the Act, or the Order in Council or the 2013 Order (as appropriate). ## SECTION I – GENERAL PROVISIONS

## Venue

## 2.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 2.1] Except as otherwise provided in paragraph 2.2, an application made to the High Court under Part 5 or Part 8 of the Act or Parts 4A and 5 of the Order in Council must be made in the Administrative Court. ## 2.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 2.2] A claim for a recovery order must be started in the Central Office of the King’s Bench Division. Where a claim for a recovery order has been issued, any interim proceedings preserving the property which is the subject of the claim will be transferred by the Administrative Court to the Central Office of the King’s Bench Division. ## 2.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 2.3] The preceding paragraph does not limit the power of the High Court to transfer claims or applications to or from the Central Office of the King’s Bench Division, Administrative Court, Chancery Division or specialist list of the High Court. ## Use of pseudonyms by staff

## 3.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 3.1] If a member of the staff of the relevant Director gives written or oral evidence in any proceedings using a pseudonym in accordance with section 449 or section 449A of the Act –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 3.1] (1) the court must be informed that the witness is using a pseudonym; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 3.1] (2) a certificate under section 449(3) or 449A(3) (as appropriate) of the Act must be filed or produced. ## SECTION II – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS UNDER PART 5 OF THE ACT OR PART 5 OF THE ORDER IN COUNCIL

## Claim for a recovery order

## 4.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.1] A claim by the enforcement authority for a recovery order must be made using the CPR Part 8 procedure. ## 4.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.2] In a claim for a recovery order based on an external order, the claim must include an application to register the external order. ## 4.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] The claim form must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (1) identify the property in relation to which a recovery order is sought;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (2) state, in relation to each item or description of property –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (a) whether the property is alleged to be recoverable property or associated property; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (b) either –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (i) who is alleged to hold the property; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (ii) where the enforcement authority is unable to identify who holds the property, the steps that have been taken to try to establish their identity;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (3) set out the matters relied upon in support of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (4) give details of the person nominated by the enforcement authority to act as trustee for civil recovery in accordance with section 267 of the Act or article 178 of the Order in Council; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.3] (5) in a claim which includes an application to register an external order, be accompanied by a copy of the external order. ## 4.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.4] The evidence in support of the claim must include the signed, written consent of the person nominated by the enforcement authority to act as trustee for civil recovery if appointed by the court. ## 4.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.5] In a claim which includes an application to register an external order, where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.5] (1) the sum specified in the external order is expressed in a currency other than sterling; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.5] (2) there are not funds held in the United Kingdom in the currency in which the sum specified is expressed sufficient to satisfy the external order,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.5] the claim form, or particulars of claim if served subsequently, must state the sterling equivalent of the sum specified. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 4.5] (Article 145(2) of the Order in Council provides that the sterling equivalent is to be calculated in accordance with the exchange rate prevailing at end of the day on which the external order is made.)

## Applications

## 5.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.1] An application for a property freezing order, an interim receiving order or a management receiving order must be made –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.1] (1) to a High Court judge; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.1] (2) in accordance with CPR Part 23. ## 5.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.2] CPR rule 23.10(2) and Sections I to V of CPR Part 25 do not apply to applications for property freezing orders, interim receiving orders and management receiving orders. ## 5.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.3] The application may be made without notice in the circumstances set out in –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.3] (1) section 245A(3) of the Act and article 147(3) of the Order in Council (in the case of an application for a property freezing order);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.3] (2) section 246(3) of the Act and article 151(3) of the Order in Council (in the case of an application for an interim receiving order); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.3] (3) section 245E of the Act and article 150A(3) of the Order in Council (in the case of an application for a management receiving order). ## 5.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.4] An application for a property freezing order must be supported by written evidence which must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.4] (1) set out the grounds on which the order is sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.4] (2) give details of each item or description of property in respect of which the order is sought, including

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.4] (a) an estimate of the value of the property; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.4] (b) the additional information referred to in paragraph 5.5(2). ## 5.5

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] CPR Part 69 (court’s power to appoint a receiver) and Practice Direction 69 apply to an application for an interim receiving order with the following modifications –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (1) paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 69 does not apply;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (2) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must, in addition to the matters required by paragraph 4.1 of that practice direction, also state in relation to each item or description of property in respect of which the order is sought –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (a) whether the property is alleged to be –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (i) recoverable property; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (ii) associated property,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] and the facts relied upon in support of that allegation; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (b) in the case of any associated property –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (i) who is believed to hold the property; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (ii) if the enforcement authority is unable to establish who holds the property, the steps that have been taken to establish their identity; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5] (3) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must always identify a nominee and include the information in paragraph 4.2 of that practice direction. ## 5.5A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5A] CPR Part 69 (court’s power to appoint a receiver) and Practice Direction 69 apply to an application for a management receiving order with the following modifications—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.5A] (1) paragraph 2.1 of Practice Direction 69 does not apply; and(2) the enforcement authority’s written evidence must always identify a nominee and include the information in paragraph 4.2 of that Practice Direction. ## 5.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5.6] Where an application is made for an interim receiving order or management receiving order, a draft of the order which is sought must be filed with the application notice. This should if possible also be supplied to the court in an electronic form compatible with the word processing software used by the court. ## 5A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5A] A property freezing order or interim receiving order which is made before a claim for a recovery order has been commenced will –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5A] (1) specify a period within which the enforcement authority must either start the claim or apply for the continuation of the order while he carries out his investigation; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5A] (2) provide that the order will be set aside if the enforcement authority does not start the claim or apply for its continuation before the end of that period. ## Exclusions when making property freezing order or interim receiving order

## 5B.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.1] When the court makes a property freezing order or interim receiving order on an application without notice, it will normally make an initial exclusion from the order for the purpose of enabling the respondent to meet his reasonable legal costs so that he may –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.1] (1) take advice in relation to the order;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.1] (2) prepare a statement of assets in accordance with paragraph 7A.3; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.1] (3) if so advised, apply for the order to be varied or set aside. [PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.1] The total amount specified in the initial exclusion will not normally exceed £3,000. ## 5B.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.2] When it makes a property freezing order or interim receiving order before a claim for a recovery order has been commenced, the court may also make an exclusion to enable the respondent to meet his reasonable legal costs so that (for example) when the claim is commenced –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.2] (1) he may file an acknowledgment of service and any written evidence on which he intends to rely; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.2] (2) he may apply for a further exclusion for the purpose of enabling him to meet his reasonable costs of the proceedings. ## 5B.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 5B.3] Paragraph 7A contains general provisions about exclusions made for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs. ## Interim receiving order or management receiving order: application for directions

## 6.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] An application for directions as to the exercise of the functions of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] (1) the interim receiver under section 251 of the Act or article 156 of the Order in Council; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] (2) the management receiver under section 245G of the Act  or article 150C of under the Order in Council,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] may be made at any time by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] (a) the interim receiver or management receiver, as appropriate;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] (b) any party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.1] (c) any person affected by any action taken, or proposed to be taken, by the interim receiver or management receiver. ## 6.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.2] The application must always be made by application notice, which must be served on –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.2] (1) the interim receiver or management receiver, as appropriate, (unless he is the applicant);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.2] (2) every party to the proceedings; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 6.2] (3) any other person who may be interested in the application. ## Application to vary or set aside an order

## 7.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.1] An application to vary or set aside a property freezing order, an interim receiving order or a management receiving order (including an application for, or relating to, an exclusion from the order) may be made at any time by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.1] (1) the enforcement authority; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.1] (2) any person affected by the order. ## 7.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2] Unless the court otherwise directs or exceptional circumstances apply, a copy of the application notice must be served on –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2] (1) every party to the proceedings;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2] (2) in the case of an application to vary or set aside an interim receiving order or management receiving order, the interim receiver or management receiver (as appropriate); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2] (3) any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision. ## 7.2A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2A] Before exercising the power to discharge or vary a property freezing order, the court must give an opportunity for the parties, and any other person who may be affected by the court’s decision, to be heard, in accordance with section 245B(5) of the Act or Article 148(5) of the Order in Council (as appropriate). ## 7.2B

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.2B] A Master or District Judge may, with the consent of all the parties, vary or discharge a property freezing order, an interim receiving order or a management receiving order granted by any Judge.”. ## 7.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] The evidence in support of an application for an exclusion from a property freezing order or interim receiving order for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] (1) contain full details of the stage or stages in civil recovery proceedings in respect of which the costs in question have been or will be incurred;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] (2) include a statement of the costs which the person has incurred and an estimation of the costs which the person will incur in relation to each stage to which the application relates;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] (3) include a statement of assets containing the information set out in paragraph 7A.3 (unless the person has previously filed such a statement in the same civil recovery proceedings, or the person has previously filed a statement of assets containing the information set out in paragraph 7H.3 (for an application for an exclusion from a prohibition order), or in paragraph 18.14 (for an application for an exclusion from an interim freezing order), and there has been no material change in the facts set out in the applicable previous statement);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] (4) where the court has previously made an exclusion in respect of any stage to which the application relates, explain why the person’s costs will exceed the amount specified in the exclusion for that stage; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3] (5) state whether the terms of the exclusion have been agreed with the enforcement authority. ## 7.3A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7.3A] Where, under paragraph 7.3(2), a person includes in evidence a statement of the costs which the person has incurred, paragraphs 9.5(2) and (3) of Practice Direction 44 apply. ## Exclusions for the purpose of meeting legal costs: general provisions

## 7A.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.1] Subject to paragraph 7A.2, when the court makes an order or gives directions in civil recovery proceedings it will at the same time consider whether it is appropriate to make or vary an exclusion for the purpose of enabling any person affected by the order or directions to meet his reasonable legal costs. ## 7A.1A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.1A] To enable the court to consider whether it is appropriate to make or vary an exclusion, the court may order a party to file an estimate of costs (unless the person has previously filed such an estimate in the same civil recovery proceedings and there has been no material change in the facts set out in that estimate). ## 7A.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION – CIVIL RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS > 7A.2] The court will not make an exclusion for the purpose of enabling a person to meet his reasonable legal costs, other than an exclusion to meet the costs of taking any of the steps referred to in paragraph 5B.1, unless that person has made , served and filed a statement of assets.
